subject: physics
title: Energy stores and systems
key_idea: Energy is kept in **stores** and moves between them when a **system** changes. It is transferred by forces doing work, by an electric current and by heating. Energy is never created or destroyed. In a closed system the total stays the same.

blocks.text: Energy is not a substance. It is kept in stores. This section covers the stores you need to name.

items.meaning: An object or a group of objects that interact.
Energy of an object because of its height above the ground.
Energy in a stretched or squashed object, such as a spring.
Energy in the particles of an object. It increases when the object gets hotter.
Energy in fuel, food and batteries, released by chemical reactions.

blocks.text: Other stores are nuclear, magnetic and electrostatic. A spinning fly wheel stores energy in its kinetic store.

items: A system is an object or a group of objects.
Name the store, such as kinetic or chemical, not just 'energy'.
A moving object, including a spinning fly wheel, has energy in its kinetic store.

blocks.text: When a system changes, energy is transferred from one store to another. There are three main ways to change the energy of a system.

items: **Work done by forces.** A force moves an object, as when you lift a toy car.
**Work done when a current flows.** Electrical equipment such as a motor transfers energy from the battery or mains.
**Heating.** Energy moves from a hotter object to a cooler one.

diagram.alt: Sort each item into an energy store or a way of changing the energy of a system.
diagram.prompt: Is it a store, or a way energy is transferred?

items.text: Work done by an electric current

rows: Kinetic store decreases. Gravitational potential store increases.
Kinetic store decreases. Thermal store of the object and surroundings increases.
Object accelerated by a constant force
Energy from the force's work increases the kinetic store.
Kinetic store decreases. Thermal store of the brakes and surroundings increases.
Kettle bringing water to the boil
Energy from the current increases the thermal store of the water.

items: Energy changes stores through work done by forces, work done by a current, or heating.
For each change, say which store decreases and which store increases.
Some energy usually ends up in the thermal store of the surroundings.

blocks.text: Energy cannot be created or destroyed. It can only be transferred, stored or dissipated.

items.meaning: A system where no energy enters or leaves.
When energy is transferred in a closed system, there is no net change to the total energy.

blocks.label: Conservation of energy
blocks.formula: total energy before = total energy after
where: Some energy moves to less useful stores, such as the thermal store of the surroundings.

blocks.text: A transfer diagram shows where energy starts, where it goes and what is wasted. Each arrow is a transfer.

diagram.alt: Energy transfers when a battery powered drone rises.
steps: Work done by current in motor
Work done by force from blades

items: At each stage, some energy is also wasted to the thermal store of the surroundings.
All energy changes are measured in joules, so stores can be compared on one scale.
The total of all the stores at the end equals the energy at the start.
A rocket that transfers 510 MJ from its fuel gains 510 MJ in its other stores.
In a closed system the total energy does not change.
Energy is conserved, so energy in equals energy out.
A transfer diagram shows each transfer and the wasted energy.

checks.q: Give two energy stores that increase when an electric whisk is switched on.
checks.a: Kinetic store of the beater and food. Thermal (internal) store of the surroundings, whisk or food.

checks.q: State what happens to the total energy when energy is transferred in a closed system.
checks.a: The total energy does not change. Energy is conserved.

checks.q: Describe the energy changes when a car brakes to a stop.
checks.a: The kinetic store of the car decreases. The thermal store of the brakes (and surroundings) increases.

worked_example.question:
Wood is burned to heat water in a pipe.
Describe the change to the stores of energy of the wood, pipe and water as the water is heated.

Wood
Pipe
Water
answer_points: The chemical store of energy of the wood decreases
The internal / thermal store of energy of the pipe increases
The internal / thermal store of energy of the water increases
worked_example.tip: Each mark needs both the store and what happens to it.

worked_example.question:
A football of mass 0.42 kg is kicked against a wall.

Describe the energy transfers that happen when the ball hits the wall.
answer_points: It transfers to one of: elastic (potential energy store), thermal (energy of ball / wall / surroundings), or dissipates (to surroundings)
worked_example.tip: One mark for the kinetic store and one for where the energy goes. Heat is allowed for thermal. Gravitational potential energy is ignored.

worked_example.question:
In the brakes of a car there are brake pads and a brake disc.
When a car stops, energy transfers between stores.
The brake pads squeeze the brake disc and cause a friction force.

Explain how braking stops the car.
Include ideas about energy stores in your answer.
answer_points: (Store of) KE (in the moving car) decreases
It is transferred thermally to the (store of) thermal energy / heat (in the brakes, pads, discs or tyres)
worked_example.tip: One mark for the kinetic store and one for the thermal store it is transferred to.
